title: Guard a while-read over a herestring with [ -n ] when the input may be empty
answers: rerun workflow calls gh run rerun with an empty id when no checks qualify
bash while read loop runs once on an empty herestring
spurious 'Failed to rerun' log in the approval rerun workflow when no jobs failed
body:
Symptom: when no check runs qualify for rerun, the approval rerun workflow logs a rerun line with no run ID and a 'Failed to rerun' message, even though nothing failed.
Root cause: .github/workflows/rerun-workflow-run.yml (rerun step, the `rows=$(...)` capture read by `while read -r id name ... done <<< "$rows"`): a herestring of an empty string still feeds one empty line to `read`, so the loop body runs once with an empty id.
Fix pattern: wrap the read loop in `if [ -n "$rows" ]; then ... fi`, so empty command output makes no `rerun` calls.
Constraints: only needed when the captured variable can be empty; non-empty output is unaffected. Applies to loops over command-substitution output in this workflow; the symptom wording is inferred from the guard's stated purpose, not a reported incident.
applies: Shell loops over captured command output in .github/workflows/rerun-workflow-run.yml only.
says: Approval rerun workflow displays a failed rerun error even though no checks failed.
Build logs show an empty job rerun attempt when all checks have already passed.
Stop logging spurious rerun failure warnings when no workflow runs require retry.
search: In .github/workflows/rerun-workflow-run.yml, wrap the while-read loop over captured command herestring rows in if [ -n "$rows" ]; then ... fi. This prevents running an iteration with an empty run ID and logging a spurious 'Failed to rerun' message when no check runs qualify. Applies only to loops over captured command-substitution output in .github/workflows/rerun-workflow-run.yml where the variable can be empty.
